q: In Railway traffic accounts, what does 'outstanding' at a station primarily mean?

options.A: Earnings realized and remitted to cash office
options.B: Earnings due but not yet collected from parties
options.D: Earnings written off by the FA&CAO

q: Which of the following commonly gives rise to outstanding at a goods station?

options.C: To-pay freight not yet collected from consignee

q: Unrealized coaching earnings at a station usually arise from which source?

options.D: Unpaid parcels, luggage and miscellaneous dues

q: Where is the record of station outstandings primarily maintained?

options.A: In the outstanding register of the station
options.D: In the station cash book only

q: The Traffic Accounts Office reviews station outstandings mainly to ensure what?

options.A: Prompt realization and no artificial inflation
options.C: Daily cash remittance of all dues

q: Station outstanding statements are rendered to the Traffic Accounts Office at what frequency?
City booking agencies function in relation to Railways primarily as what?

options.D: Outstations collecting fares and freight on behalf of Railways

q: Earnings collected by a city booking agency are accounted for as which type?

options.A: Traffic earnings credited through the agency's account

q: Outstandings at a city booking agency must be settled within the period fixed in which document?

options.A: The agency agreement with the Railway

q: What security arrangement normally backs a city booking agency's outstandings?
Review of outstandings by the Traffic Accounts Office involves comparison with which record?

options.C: Station balance sheets and previous statements

q: An outstanding carried forward month after month without recovery action is treated as what?

options.A: An item needing special review and possible write-off
options.C: A credit to the party's account

q: Write-off of irrecoverable outstandings requires sanction of which authority?

options.B: The competent financial authority as per delegation

q: Before proposing a write-off of an outstanding, what must the Railway establish?

options.A: That the station wants a clean register
options.C: That all recovery efforts have failed and the amount is irrecoverable
options.D: That the party has moved abroad

q: Which document supports a write-off proposal of station outstandings?

options.B: A copy of the time table
options.C: A memorandum showing recovery efforts and reasons for irrecoverability

q: Demurrage and wharfage charges not collected before delivery of wagons appear as what?
In goods accounts, 'unrealized earnings' differ from 'outstandings' in that they refer to what?

options.A: Earnings not yet brought to account or collected

q: The station balance sheet shows outstandings under which classification?
Which officer at the station is primarily responsible for pursuing outstandings?

options.C: The station master / in-charge of commercial work

q: Credit notes or credit facilities allowed to regular customers create which risk?
A proper review of outstandings includes checking the age-wise analysis to identify what?

options.A: Fresh and old items needing differentiated action

q: Outstandings pertaining to military or government traffic are followed up through which channel?

options.C: Special bills and correspondence with the concerned department

q: When a consignee refuses delivery, the freight already due becomes what?

options.D: An outstanding pending disposal of goods

q: Sale of unclaimed or refused goods at auction first adjusts which amount?

options.A: Railway dues outstanding against the consignment

q: Unrealized earnings of the coaching department do NOT include which item?
The Traffic Accounts Office raises debits against stations for what purpose?

options.C: To bring to account earnings short-collected or omitted

q: Station outstandings shown inflated due to fictitious entries indicate which problem?

options.D: Fraud or defective accounting needing investigation

q: Reconciliation of city booking agency accounts is done with which returns?

options.D: Agency's periodical returns of bookings and remittances

q: Commission payable to a city booking agency is calculated on what basis?

options.B: The agreed percentage on earnings collected through the agency

q: If a city booking agency defaults on remittance, the Railway first resorts to which step?

options.C: Recovery from the agency's security deposit

q: Outstanding on account of 'siding charges' arises at stations serving which facility?

options.C: Private sidings using railway wagons and facilities

q: The periodical review of outstandings by divisional officers aims to achieve what?

options.B: Transfer of dues to another division
options.D: Reduction of old outstandings through targeted recovery

q: Which statement best describes a 'write-off' in railway accounts?

options.A: Recording an irrecoverable amount as a loss with proper sanction
options.C: Transferring dues to the next year

q: After write-off, if the amount is subsequently recovered, how is it treated?

options.C: Credited as miscellaneous earnings of the year of recovery

q: Suspense heads in traffic accounts are used for which purpose?

options.C: Parking amounts pending final adjustment or clarification

q: Prolonged balances under suspense heads relating to outstandings indicate what?
Which report helps the FA&CAO monitor the overall position of outstandings?

options.A: The consolidated statement of outstandings from TAO

q: Outstandings against other railways arising from interchanged traffic are settled through which mechanism?

options.C: Inter-railway financial adjustments through accounts offices

q: A 'debit' raised by TAO against a station for undercharge becomes what at the station?

options.C: An outstanding to be recovered from the party

q: Which of the following reduces station outstandings?

options.D: Actual recovery of dues from parties

q: Coaching outstandings at big stations are most often connected with which traffic?

options.D: Retiring room bookings paid in advance

q: The outstanding register at a station should show which details for each item?

options.B: Date, party, amount, nature of due and recovery action

q: Internal check of outstandings by accounts inspectors focuses on what?

options.C: Genuineness, ageing and action taken on each item

q: Which authority fixes the credit limit for parties allowed credit facilities?

options.D: The competent commercial authority per delegation

q: Exceeding the sanctioned credit limit by a party should result in what?

options.B: Stoppage of further credit bookings till dues are cleared

q: Unrealized earnings shown in traffic accounts affect which financial statement?

options.B: The revenue account as dues not yet realized

q: A city booking agency's daily takings must be remitted to the Railway within what?

options.C: The time limit prescribed in the agreement

q: Short remittance by a city booking agency detected on reconciliation is treated as what?

options.D: A recoverable outstanding against the agency

q: Which of these is a valid ground for write-off of an outstanding?

options.D: Desire for a clean register at year end

q: Write-off sanctions must be supported by which financial concurrence?

options.B: Concurrence of the associated finance as per rules

q: Outstandings written off without competent sanction are viewed by audit as what?

options.D: An irregularity and possible loss to be regularized

q: The Traffic Accounts Office clears station outstandings from its books only when what happens?

options.D: The station reports recovery, adjustment or sanctioned write-off

q: Which type of outstanding is considered most difficult to recover?

options.A: Dues against parties who are untraceable or insolvent

q: To prevent accumulation of outstandings, stations are expected to do what?

options.B: Collect dues promptly and pursue defaulters vigorously

q: Demurrage charges accrue when wagons are detained beyond which period?

options.C: The free time allowed for loading or unloading

q: Wharfage charges are levied for detention of goods beyond free time at which place?
Uncollected demurrage at the time of wagon release is recorded in which register?
Rebate or waiver of demurrage claimed by parties is decided by which authority?

options.B: The competent commercial authority per delegation

q: Outstanding freight on 'paid' traffic is unusual because freight is normally collected when?
Which check helps detect fictitious outstandings at stations?

options.D: Verification of outstanding items with original documents

q: City booking agencies also handle which ancillary service for Railways?

options.B: Booking of passengers, luggage and parcels in the city

q: The Railway's liability for tickets issued by a city booking agency is the same as for what?
Excess remittance by a city booking agency is dealt with by which action?

options.C: Adjustment or refund as per the agreement

q: Outstanding statements of stations are scrutinized in TAO with reference to what?

options.D: Balance sheets, registers and previous correspondence

q: A sudden rise in outstandings at a station calls for which immediate step?

options.A: Detailed inquiry into causes and special recovery drive

q: Which document authorizes a station to keep dues outstanding instead of collecting cash?

options.B: A credit note or sanctioned credit arrangement

q: Unrealized earnings from 'to-pay' parcels are realized at which point?

options.D: At the time of delivery against payment

q: The ultimate responsibility for clearance of traffic outstandings rests with which organization?

options.D: The Traffic Accounts Office in coordination with commercial departments

q: Which of the following best summarizes the objective of outstanding review?

options.A: To maximize long-pending dues on books
options.B: To ensure every due is genuine, pursued and cleared or written off properly

q: In the station balance sheet, a fall in outstandings without corresponding remittance suggests what?

options.B: Possible unauthorized write-off or adjustment needing inquiry
